verdict.tagline: Deep engineering freedom hidden behind a punishing and broken tutorial.
for_you_if: you love building complex machinery from scratch
you have patience for steep learning curves
not_for_you_if: you expect a functional in-game tutorial
you want smooth performance without crashes

distortion_flags.sentence: Player sentiment shifts positively as playtime increases from initial frustration to long-term engagement.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the built-in tutorial as broken or non-functional, noting that basic tasks fail to register completion or cause soft-locks.

citations.review_text:
The tutorial does not function at a technical level.
- The 'run through the basic controls' tasks don't reliably register that you've done them. A switch-to-third-person-mode task doesn't register while you're still in the vehicle that you started in, without the tutorial giving you any indication that you're supposed to leave the vehicle at that point.
- Tells you to toggle something while flying. I took a couple seconds longer at a previous task, so I'm out of fuel and can't fly anymore. No instructions on how to refuel included. Guess I'll restart and try to speed run the previous steps so I can actually do the tutorial.
- "go mine some stuff and pick the rocks". I pick up the rocks, tutorial does not register that I've done that. No idea what wonky side-condition I'm missing this time, but at this point I've run out of patience. A game is supposed to be about having fun, not about getting frustrated at bugs. Refund it is.
HUGE  disapointment! to build something proper you basically need every dlc and the tutorial is just bad and sometimes won;t even work, i do not reccomend.

what is the point of this game. I went into the tutorial mission and couldnt get past the basic stuff. It was telling me pre hold alt and scroll when alt was bound to crouch, have they HARD TYPED the instructions rather than getting them to refer to a keybind reference? It also said I need to do a recharge at a kit, without telling me what or where a kit is, there are tanks in one place but no tanks in the other and I cant put tanks in the other? I have no idea what the tutorial wanted me to do. I went onto youtube to watch someone else and try to follow them, they said skip the tutorial it doesnt work, follow me instead. I tried to, but foudn the game so unnecessarily convoluted that I have uninstalled it. After 30 mins I couldnt figure out how to stop the buggy from rolling off down a hill every time I got out, and couldnt figure out how to even equip the gun you are given. Why have they made this game some completely inaccessible???? I wish to high heaven I didnt buy it, feels like an early access game where they havent even got their ♥♥♥♥ together yet.

Never have I ever given a bad review to a game.

Well, today's the day.

The tutorial kept on soft-locking me, or whatever it is, "Quick-start". Couldn't understand how to destroy stuff for the first 10 minutes. The trailer was SO different from this "garbage".

I was expecting something like trailmakers + no man's sky + stellaris. This was so much worse.

I couldn't figure out how to move building blocks, because the tutorial was terrible. I couldn't... for the life of me, figure out how I was so excited about this before I bought it.

Building makes me want to refund the game, which I most probably will! 90% of the game is behind two thousand DLCs. I bought three, and I only unlocked like, 13 building blocks or, whatever the hell.

3/10, I do NOT recommend this game.

Too grindy and full of jank. It's so grindy that the default settings for survival mode are 3x resource output. The tutorial doesn't inform you that some of the components are broken, and need to be fixed to complete the tutorial. The hand drilling is janky, requiring you to stop drilling every second to collect each individual rock.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that rovers struggle on small slopes and lack recovery options when flipped.

citations.review_text:
Tutorial: *warns you that wheeled vehicles flip easily
Also Tutorial: *does not tell you what to do if a vehicle flips
Also Tutorial: *gives you mission waypoint over rugged terrain
Vehicle: *inevitably flips
Tutorial: ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

13 years in development!

It's impossible to learn how to do anything when all the mechanics are so opaque and the recommended starting spawn drops you in the middle of nowhere dozens of kilometers away from anyone you might be playing the game with, with a rover that can't handle the smallest of slopes and has no way to get back up if it flips. It might be interesting to play in singleplayer if you can handle the obtuseness and the tutorial being incredibly poorly designed, but if you are gifted this game by someone else who wants to play it with you like I was, I recommend you refust the gift or refund the game and get them their money back. I'll more than likely be doing that soon enough.

claims.claim: Reviewers report issues with the user interface, citing poor contrast, missing inventory elements, and difficulty with key rebinding.

citations.review_text:
Game has one of the worst UIs I've ever used. Rebinding keys doesn't work (tab key for inventory for example - and no mouse thumb buttons), ZERO notification when you are unlocking components - and the screen showing your progression has basically zero difference between the locked and unlocked icon - apparently they are supposed to be slightly greyed out, but if you don't know what the look like in the first place... ???

You can't use items from your inventory or move items to your hot bar - in fact it actually disappears when you are in your inventory for... reasons?

That and zero in game tutorials or even tooltips is just absurd. 

Unless you want to watch like hours of videos to learn this game, don't bother picking it up...

It seems interesting. And I really wanted to play it. Has dept, and complexity, and looks like a lot of fun for a builder etc.  Really  cool concept.  I would say give it a shot.  But i did return it however, as unfortunately I couldn't get through the "quick start" tutorial.  1) It wasn't progressing or responding to input, 2) I found it really difficult to view given a lack of good contrast between text and the background.  This is unfortunate for me, because I really wanted to like and play this game. It looks amazing.  But impossible, for me, to read.   45 minutes to cover what should have been 2 minutes of the tutorial (basic movement and interface familiarity).  I asked for a refund.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from crashes and performance lag.

citations.review_text: Wanted to play space engineers from all the cool videos and recommendations over the years, instead played "manual mining drill and Computer crash simulator".  In addition, the tutorial says to do something but doesn't tell you how.
Fun, a bit laggy on my pc but my specs are low so i dont blame the game

So far  here are the pros and cons.  

Pros:
* Massive open world building game
* Relatively chill environment
* Mild combat potential (we'll see how this plays out later).
* Tons of building parts and build progression and thus options
* More of a hard Sci Fi feel than Science Opera

Cons:
* Sometimes tends to randomly lag
* Has on occasion lagged my entire rig so I can't do much of anything else until after I quit the game.
* The connector system is weird as are the block rotation controls.
* Very complex build system.   Sometimes its hard to know what connects to what and what is needed for what.   You are going to watch  a lot of tutorials.
* Don't die without a survival kit.  Survival kit = Respawns.   No survival kit = Hardcore mode (and its harder to make stuff as well.)

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the in-game tutorial is unhelpful, missing, or fails to properly explain core systems and controls.

citations.review_text: Wanted to play space engineers from all the cool videos and recommendations over the years, instead played "manual mining drill and Computer crash simulator".  In addition, the tutorial says to do something but doesn't tell you how.

I want to like this game but... Holy moly... It's extremely complicated and nothing is explained well or thoroughly.

This game actually takes twelve hour series just to learn the *controls.*

I always hate giving indie games negative reviews, but... every single crafting recipe requiring large multi-step lists of way too many different types of parts is just too much.

And there's little to no gameplay.

Absolutely ridiculous.  10 years later and still no scroll to change weapon, tab to open inventory, no tutorial, quick start is basically minecraft without any of the fun.  I was an early supporter, but apparently i velieved in the game more than the developers did.

Directionless. Unguided. Left to drift. Tutorial "bot" wastes 2 hours making player do WASD and jetpack circus tricks, sends you off to drill for rocks, then leaves you figure out how to build the first block it wants.

The YouTube videos in the Help are over 7 years old with visuals, screens, and menus also from 7 years ago.
I cant find a tutorial and this game is crazy complex

First impressions. Game feels like more complicated clone of "Empyrion - Galactic Survival". No compass at planet surface. To start gaming u need to watch youtube coz tutorial in the game not the best.

Ended up having to gather from many sources for a basic starter tutorial (one good tutorial for PC is https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TZxEVe2H_Gs&list=PLfMGCUepUcNy2XHRLrGo0Dqsg86E7D3og by Splitsie).

Then again, by following the above tutorial in the quick start scenario, it takes an hour of stone mining just to get the basic refinery and assembler going. Maybe the sandbox mode is the way to go with the game.
Does not have a new player friendly tutorial. The tutorial explains very little as to how to operate the controls and interfaces.

The game is vastly empty. Planet side you might see a wolf or two. The crafting system is overly complicated. There is no tutorial or any sort of explanation as to how to do anything other than a screen pop up that tells you to do something, but does not explain how to do it. If you have time to waste, and you just want to explore an empty word, then go for it, might be for you. I personally found this game to be incredibly boring and tedious.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that playing multiplayer with friends is cumbersome, specifically citing issues with spawn locations and server connectivity.

citations.review_text: Do not buy.  There is no spawn on friends.  I don't want a commute in a game played for fun.  You wasted an hour of my time driving to a friend tonight.  You spawned me on another planet.  Too much time, trying to get to my friend.  Does not respect my time.  Other than that.  Physics based game.  Procedurally generated.  Terrain generation is frustrating.  It will generate undrivable areas.  It will spawn you 50km or more from party members in their own world.  Do not waste your time.  Single player, sure, have at it.  Not worth playing with friends because you spend all your time commuting.  How do you not have this solved?
bought this to play cross plat with a friend just to find out its only possible through public dedicated servers which defeated the purpose of buying this game

This game is so beginner-unfriendly it's insane. I wanted to try this game with a friend, but little did I know it would be a nightmare to even figure out how to do that. You can't do the tutorials maps OR quick start with a friend. You HAVE to create a new game, and you're presented with so many options you don't even have a clue which one is the right one to pick. Then you get into the game, and you have no idea how to even find your friend. I literally had to go to the internet to figure it out because this game is so convoluted. Ended up spending nearly 3 hours not even playing the game, just trying to figure out how things work and trying to find my friend on the map.

I bet this game can be fun, but only after you've taken an entire educational course on how to play it. Honestly can't believe I wasted my money on this garbage game that doesn't care about or even understand a new player.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the survival mode as lacking objectives, direction, or meaningful substance beyond building ships and gathering resources.

citations.review_text:
I unironically made my friend buy it, because I thought it would be more fun to play in two - no, it really wasn't. Biggest mistake I've ever made. As it turns out, despite being out for well over 7 years now, the developers still continue treating this game as nothing but a tech demo. The survival is completely devoid of any objectives, at all. They even tried to pull a fell for it again moment by releasing a second one of these, with - you guessed it - EVEN LESS TO DO. And people ate it up. The customer base Keen have cultivated here is really depressing to watch. But I guess you could sell a jar of ♥♥♥♥ if you have the right story to go alongside it.

This game will really only appeal to you if you either enjoy making people who don't deserve it rich - or if you've hit yourself on the head as a kid enough times to actually enjoy the concept of a sandbox survival game where the only thing to do is gathering random ores for not very much reason at all, and building ships and stations out of them - again, for not very much reason at all. Minecraft in space my ass. This thing has less real survival content (what SovietWomble would call "fluff") than a vibecoded Minecraft clone.

Seriously though, don't buy this. Setting 20 bucks on fire will give you more entertainment than this game.

Effectively just a huge tech demo with absolutely nothing to do in survival, at all. Unless you're autistic and spend thousands of hours just building ships and crashing them into other ships, of course.

Honestly wish i could enjoy this game but there is to much wrong with it to recommend it to anyone. 

Yet another set of greedy ass developers selling an already expensive and overpriced game full of cosmetics and locking 90% of the building pieces behind paid "DLC's". If i dont own the blocks they shouldn't be in my building menu to begin with because i dont want to try and build a ship just to see basically all of the buildings are locked behind a paywall. 

Trying to figure out what to actually play to learn the game is about the same as trying to find a needle at the core of the earth. There is absolutely no direction on which mode to actually play and the only reason i was able to figure out which one was a good start was from watching a video from an already established player. 

After actually figure out what your supposed to do to actually play the game its an insane slog fest trying to actually get your first real ship up and running. and after having read some other reviews and the comments under them there is no reason you should require 50 hours just to get your first ship up and running. With so much to explore of the vast nothingness once your off the planet there is not really much to do other than build more ships. The only interesting way I've seen this game played was full of mods which really says a lot about how poorly made this game really is.

While i wish i could find more positive things about it the only thing i can really say is it does have a decent community that builds some pretty awesome things. Which is sad because a game like this would really be something id be able to drop thousands of hours in but with the lack of any direction and the fact its yet another game with devs who abuse the DLC system to feed their endless greed i refuse to support this game anymore in any way.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that automated docking mechanisms and AI recorders fail to function reliably without community scripts or complex workarounds.

citations.review_text:
After all these years there still is not even a semi-reliable way to make a ship dock automatically.

The official solution is the AI Recorder: record a waypoint at the connector, add a connection action, and hope the ship gets close enough. In my experience, in non-zero gravity, it stops too far away from the connector at least every other time, tries to connect once, fails, and then simply ends the sequence. Game over. No more autonomous whatever it was supposed to do. It does not check whether docking actually worked, move closer, realign, or try again.

So the player has to build workarounds with repeated waypoints and Event Controllers, write a complete docking controller, or use a community script just to make any automated craft dock.

For a game built around spacecrafts, engineering and automation, that is an insanely basic thing to be missing while they tell you to buy Space Engineers 2.

[h2]Pros[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
You can build truly epic structures, vehicles, and spaceships (but doing so outside of Creative Mode is a complete nightmare).

[h2]Cons[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
[b]Graphics:[/b]
- There is definitely something wrong with the lighting and shadow system. Everything looks very weird. The image also feels blurry (and FXAA antialiasing isn't the culprit here). Tweaking the settings doesn't fix it. Mods partially solve this issue.

[b]Controls:[/b]
- Most building games and MMOs have long adopted a somewhat standardized control scheme optimized for inventory management and hotbars. Here, the controls are as clunky as it gets, and in most cases, you can't even fix it by rebinds. Some actions can't be rebound at all.
- If you are standing right up against an object, you can't jump onto it, which is incredibly annoying when building (i get that it's tied to how the game's physics work, but when you can't even jump up a tiny ledge, it just looks incredibly stupid).

[b]Environment:[/b]
- Forget about decent enemies (proper PvE is non-existent). They are as dumb as a brick. I want to highlight the wolves specifically rather than space battles. They spawn right behind your back when you spend too much time working in one spot (on Earth like planets). What’s absurd isn’t just that they spawn out of nowhere, but how they behave and move. Since it’s a building sandbox, it’s somewhat forgivable, but still. For the reason mentioned above, the game is only worth playing either with someone else (just to spend a few evenings building your dream ship and chatting) or against other players (if you enjoy PvP).

citations.review_text: really fun spaceship/station building system with extreme creative freedom hidden behind the worst tutorial ever and extremely unintuitive menus. i love it

This game is incredibly rough to get into, and it disrespects the players time at every step of the way. 

Just booting into the game, you get a whole laundry list of DLCs and a bare bones menu that points you to a 'quick start' option. Pressing that jumps you into a game with a tutorial text box explaining the basic controls. That tutorial text box bugged out multiple times while I was playing, showing a brief tutorial before changing to a blank text box before I completed that section of the tutorial. 

I basically wandered around lost for hours before I gave up and tried to look help online. The SE subreddit pointed to a youtube tutorial for beginners, and while that one was helpful, it's a horrible look when the gamedevs can't be arsed to guide new players properly before releasing 19! DLCs.

Even pushing past this, the game UX is awful. Searching for items from a conveyor system is terrible and requires the player to constantly either scroll up and down for a randomly ordered list of containers, or take their hands off the mouse for the search bar. The build planner for pulling resources out of storage is limited to 8 items, so when I want to build something its a slog to build it all out, then go back to the beginning and build the first 8 items and so on. Trying to figure out why an item inventory shows up in my grid but I can't interact with it is a pain in the ass and is infuriating.

I'm sure there are 'better' ways to interact with the game that I'm missing as a new player, but when there are this many roadblocks to the start of this game, its just not worth continuing to learn.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the food and survival mechanics as frustratingly balanced, noting that food sources are extremely scarce or locked behind late-tech items.

citations.review_text: It's boring and overly complicated. I have never gotten past the most basic levels cause I can never get enough resources or food. The only things I can build are in creative mode. The actual game is unplayable for me. Many like it, but I don't. I normally enjoy these games and have found this one boring and frustrating. It also gets bogged down and I have to restart the game to restore function. It seems random.

So the game is pretty good, its excellent and I'll keep playing. Due to how food is impossible to get and garentees 'prepare to die and starve for a few lives' edition, it gets a thumbs down till the day that's fixed. 

What's going on is plants spawn so far apart that you can't eat and find them before you die, they act more as a trophy for exploring.. which is emptier than Starfields planets no joke. (Lets not worry about that though, the crafting makes up for blank worlds by far, beating Starfield on a large margine). So plant density should at a minimum be an option in the menu. 

Secondly, they put the food processor at the top of the tech tree which is the first method to get food. So you have to build an algae station first which is a late game structure in all games you might play, because that's infinite food. Food processor is basically a campfire. Imagine playing 7 days to die, and the campfire is late game, the wolf meat or spider meat in this game is garenteed poison, you just die, its not a debuff. You go to 0 food, and it kills you. You need the top tech tree food processor to cook it. The algae station will kill you if you spend the entire beginning sitting at the start of where you spawned trying to craft it. You die. 

The youtube videos are telling you to destroy your rover, butcher it, rush an algae station but the game emphasizes keeping your constructed stuff alive and in good condition. Its a really bad game loop for food. 

I found the rest of it completely fun and balanced. Hydrogen, Oxygen, Power, Fuel, etc, all of the other stuff is completely my fault if I fail, but managing food early game is 'Prepare to die' or be desperate and blow up your rover or get lucky. 

The method is to spam respawn until the rover is descent starting you off with 10 rations of food. Seriously I'm restarting, this is bs. I will do a full 'setup all my mods and settings' for 5 minutes, wait 2 minutes to load, and check my inventory. If I don't see rations, I'll …

It is a great game! If you know what you are doing. I have seen videos of people building massive space ships, the actual building is fun but when it comes to some of the logic,,, 
I cant figure it out! I tried to set up some turrets to shoot stuff I lock onto, and hour and a half later I still couldn't get it too work! I'm sure its a great game but im not willing to spend 40 hours learning how it wokrs.

Good game but hard to learn

claims.claim: Reviewers state that controller support is non-functional and poorly implemented.

citations.review_text:
Controller support is a complete joke. Has options for it, but its implementation is on par with something i'd expect from a middleschooler trying to learn to code.... Its non functional. Not going to waste my time trying to debug controller support, or figure out how to rebind all of the controls, reorganize UI elements etc JUST to play with a controller...

Waste of money. Waste of time. 

0/10 - Would rather gouge my eyes out with a rusty fork then spend anymore time trying to play this dumpster fire.

[h2]Pros[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
You can build truly epic structures, vehicles, and spaceships (but doing so outside of Creative Mode is a complete nightmare).

[h2]Cons[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
[b]Graphics:[/b]
- There is definitely something wrong with the lighting and shadow system. Everything looks very weird. The image also feels blurry (and FXAA antialiasing isn't the culprit here). Tweaking the settings doesn't fix it. Mods partially solve this issue.

[b]Controls:[/b]
- Most building games and MMOs have long adopted a somewhat standardized control scheme optimized for inventory management and hotbars. Here, the controls are as clunky as it gets, and in most cases, you can't even fix it by rebinds. Some actions can't be rebound at all.
- If you are standing right up against an object, you can't jump onto it, which is incredibly annoying when building (i get that it's tied to how the game's physics work, but when you can't even jump up a tiny ledge, it just looks incredibly stupid).

[b]Environment:[/b]
- Forget about decent enemies (proper PvE is non-existent). They are as dumb as a brick. I want to highlight the wolves specifically rather than space battles. They spawn right behind your back when you spend too much time working in one spot (on Earth like planets). What’s absurd isn’t just that they spawn out of nowhere, but how they behave and move. Since it’s a building sandbox, it’s somewhat forgivable, but still. For the reason mentioned above, the game is only worth playing either with someone else (just to spend a few evenings building your dream ship and chatting) or against other players (if you enjoy PvP).

claims.claim: Reviewers state that a significant portion of building blocks and features are locked behind paid downloadable content.

citations.review_text:
Honestly wish i could enjoy this game but there is to much wrong with it to recommend it to anyone. 

Yet another set of greedy ass developers selling an already expensive and overpriced game full of cosmetics and locking 90% of the building pieces behind paid "DLC's". If i dont own the blocks they shouldn't be in my building menu to begin with because i dont want to try and build a ship just to see basically all of the buildings are locked behind a paywall. 

Trying to figure out what to actually play to learn the game is about the same as trying to find a needle at the core of the earth. There is absolutely no direction on which mode to actually play and the only reason i was able to figure out which one was a good start was from watching a video from an already established player. 

After actually figure out what your supposed to do to actually play the game its an insane slog fest trying to actually get your first real ship up and running. and after having read some other reviews and the comments under them there is no reason you should require 50 hours just to get your first ship up and running. With so much to explore of the vast nothingness once your off the planet there is not really much to do other than build more ships. The only interesting way I've seen this game played was full of mods which really says a lot about how poorly made this game really is.

While i wish i could find more positive things about it the only thing i can really say is it does have a decent community that builds some pretty awesome things. Which is sad because a game like this would really be something id be able to drop thousands of hours in but with the lack of any direction and the fact its yet another game with devs who abuse the DLC system to feed their endless greed i refuse to support this game anymore in any way.
The game is great, but a lot of the blocks/features are locked behind a paywall which is annoying when you are trying to make complex builds

claims.claim: Reviewers report that save files can grow quite large and suffer from corruption issues.

citations.review_text:
I've played for a few hours. (lol)

This game is in my top 3 favorite games of all time. Specifically, the multiplayer servers, which vary wildly in content but are all equally amazing. 

You ever have that itch of playing a game where you start with literally nothing, and through your own two hands, you build up to the point where you're commanding fleets of starships? Well this is the game for you. 

I've been a Belter in the Expanse universe through this game. I've been an officer aboard a Starfleet ship, in this game. I've been a smuggler in the Star Wars universe, I've been a trader in the Stargate universe. 

This game is amazing, and is underrated. 

It has a learning curve, yes. But there are resources, discord channels, and innumerable guides available all over. It's honestly not overly complicated, even when you get into things like scripts and mods, which are both widely available and well-supported. 

The only downsides to this game is the fact that, due to it's age, it's limited in scope to a degree. Save files can get rather large, and MP servers require frequent restarts, typically once every few hours. 

But as that's pretty much my only gripes about the game? You can see how nearly perfect it is. 

If you haven't played it, do so. While Space Engineers 2 is currently being developed and is already available - it is a completely different game in many ways, and still very early access. 

This game is... an experience.

I like this game but i think it's lacking a few things. Using your blueprints is a very difficult process that requires a lot of work, skill and can go wrong in many ways. The game doesn't even show you the cost of blueprints and there aren't any ways of building ships with multiple moving parts that don't require you to build a lot of them from scratch. It could really use a new way of bulding a ship. The logic system in this game is divided into two things - basic blocks that can only perform actions out of a limited selection and can't do complex things. And the other one is a programmable block that runs actual code in C#, locked behind settings, not available in many multiplayer servers and there's no description in game of how it actually works. It would very nice if the developers added a block based programming language that doesn't require software engineering skills like many other engineering games. I also had save file corruptions several times. The first one was when the power vent out but i was able to restore it from a backup, the second time it was when i enabled experemental mode and downloaded two popular mods from the workshop, none of which should have been able to cause that as the settings warnings said and this the files could be opened half the time which made backup system owerwrite older backups with the corrupted ones that eventually became fully corrupted. i only kept my creative world because i created multiple copies of the same save file. 
Space engineers is a very fun game but it lacks user friendliness and has occasional save file curruption problems

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that mods can conflict with one another or cause the game to crash.

citations.review_text:
I've played 2800 hours of this game. 
I had a lot of fun. I always hoped that after each update the game would develop. For so many years, updates with a few new elements were just released each time and somehow the game remained empty. With the last update, I was hoping to see something new, some life and direction in this game. 
There are hundreds of people who make mods and improve the game so that it is more diverse and complete. Somehow the creators of the game did not want to improve things. 
For example, there is a water surface mod that makes the game even more multi-layered, There is a huge variety of planets that are many times nicer than the original ones, there are hundreds of weapon mods that look many times better than the original ones, there is a mod for realistic planetary systems and gravity that give a lot of realism, there is a mod for creating bots that help or do some things in the game and this breathes some life ... the creators of the game did not want to do anything. 
The mods are nice but they are unstable sometimes and the game crashes... 
However, they chose the other option which is actually a business model that just brings them money.
 They release updates with some supposedly new elements and just take money... if you want to play and are interested you just have to buy DLC. 
Not only that, they created Space Engineers 2 which is many times better in terms of vision and which will feature liquid water, which no one has created in a game before. 
All good things, however, this constant payment for DLC and dropping drops to satisfy curiosity has already lost me. I'm finishing this game. I paid enough. This game has been dying since Space Engineers 2 started. I will watch the second version and if the game develops so slowly and with countless DLCs... I will simply never install it.

Easily worth the money, Will continue to get updates ect, mods can conflict alot harder than I remember is the only downside i can think of off the top of my head. Love this Game. 

potential for the second game is amazing if the mods and content can match this game!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks hand-holding or in-game tutorials explaining core mechanics, requiring external guides and YouTube tutorials to learn.

citations.review_text: Started with a friend, hated it due to me not knowing what to do.  Watched  Splitsie on youtube, got inspired, started building, kept building.  This game will not hold your hand at all, you learn by making mistakes and praying to KLANG that things don't explode.  Every time I restart a save I build better, and bigger!   Will keep building until the next game launches...then I will build some more!

I found this game partially by accident when I found it on the Steam. My friend that I know told me that he had played it before, but had struggled to learn how to play the game (he flew out of orbit with his jetpack only, along with scrapping his entire survival rover down, FAH). Looking at the game at the time, I 
had a feeling this was a game that I would love to the core. So, I waited for a Steam sale to buy the game. When it was discounted and I finally bought the game, I had understood why my friend severely struggled to understand the mechanics of this game. Though, him and I eventually began to understand the game after looking at online tutorials (I did all of the research and taught him, along with some of my other friends who bought the game, the basics).
 Realizing the potential of the game that was something I had been longing for (ever since I've had a computer), I eventually convinced my other friends to buy the game. It was me believing that they would use their very intelligent minds and patience that I thought they would enjoy the game, and it would be something we would have fun with as we tried out different things. Little did I know, they didn't see my vision.
 One of the first worlds I created was in creative that started on the Earth-like. I taught them the basics and they eventually figured out how to make ships of their own (Remember creative mode, ill talk about it later). I then decided to try out survival mode starting on an earthlike, and I encouraged my friends to join and try it out. One problem that makes many beginner engineers quit the game is early game survival. I didn't think much of the repetitive mining, although reflecting back on it now, I realize that it was very tedious. This is the part they didn't like much. They liked the creative game mode where you can instantly build a ship or whatever they desired. When playing survival, they felt that the process of getting materials to build a single block was too much. Eventually,…

very fun game especialy if you have a couple friends and play online. fair warning though it is a game with a bit of a learning cliff. but if your willing to watch some tutorials on youtube to get the basics down the game really opens up. ive got 500 hrs and i still learning new things. strongly recomend if your looking for a si-fi style survival

claims.claim: Reviewers note that blueprint placement is a difficult process that lacks visible resource costs.

citations.review_text:
500hrs+ and I would love to recommend this game. The game itself is fun but in recent years it has become plagued by the DLC.

I'm not even against the DLCs even despite the fact this game is slowly becoming The Sims 4. Its the fact that if you choose not to buy them the game will still try to shove them down your throat in a pretty scummy way. Normally in most games if you do not own the DLC you play the game without the extra content, in Space Engineers however that content is still in the base game you are just restricted from placing it.

Here's why this is a problem:

1. Say you buy a ship at a station, or you find a cool crashed ship, or attack one and disable it hoping you can repair it and take it over as your own. Well think again... the really great part about this game is that most if not all the ships in the base game use DLC blocks which you cannot rebuild when destroyed or missing without owning the DLCs. I think you see the problem now.

Even if you manage to get the ship without breaking a single DLC block (for example you buy it from a station), you better never let one of those DLC blocks break, because you will never be able to replace these... unless you buy the DLC that is...

Ship gets destroyed or damaged? Want to build another one? Well once again you cannot, even if you save it as a blueprint because the game wont let you place the DLC blocks, which for some reason are out there in the base game.

2. This one is minor but the UI is cluttered with all the DLC blocks. Don't own the DLC? All its blocks are still there just greyed out making finding stuff you can place very annoying. The cool thing is that there already is a system in the game for hiding stuff you cannot place in the form of a progression system.

If you don't have a block unlocked in your progression system its excluded from the UI. But if you don't have the DLC you'd expect the same exclusion to apply but nah, let them see everything they are missing out on!

And the other one is a programmable block that runs actual code in C#, locked behind settings, not available in many multiplayer servers and there's no description in game of how it actually works. It would very nice if the developers added a block based programming language that doesn't require software engineering skills like many other engineering games. I also had save file corruptions several times. The first one was when the power vent out but i was able to restore it from a backup, the second time it was when i enabled experemental mode and downloaded two popular mods from the workshop, none of which should have been able to cause that as the settings warnings said and this the files could be opened half the time which made backup system owerwrite older backups with the corrupted ones that eventually became fully corrupted. i only kept my creative world because i created multiple copies of the same save file.
